item.title: Valkyries parade wasn't just about sports. It was a celebration of who we are. All of us
item.description: Golden State Valkyries' Gabby Williams, center, celebrates with fans along the The Embarcadero during the team's WNBA Championship parade in San Francisco, Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle) Did anyone go to school? Did anyone go to work? Did anyone stop smiling? It sure didn't feel like it on a sun-splashed, joyous Wednesday afternoon, when the Bay Area showed up and showed out for their newest champions, their newest local icons. The Golden State Valkyries championship parade, like almost everything the team has done in its brief lifetime, felt flawless, unique and perfectly Bay Area. A uniting, inclusive, delightful bolt of energy. The event was a mashup of an impromptu holiday, Pride parade, women's empowerment festival, Too Short concert, Blue Wave bash and - oh yeah - a sports title celebration. "It's like a movie," said Peter Guber, the team's part owner and a successful film producer. He was looking out over a cinematic scene, as the Valkyries ferry boat pulled out of the port at Jack London Square, and began the trip from Oakland to San Francisco across the sparkling bay waters. Iconic setting. Legendary characters. Spectacular story. Everything about this team has been intentional, well thought out, from the start. And the victory celebration was no exception. It united all our disparate parts, our proud identities, our different cities. It highlighted what is uniquely us . And the day after much of the nation rejected the current regime's divisive agenda, it was a feel-good, validating celebration. Though most in the throngs that lined the Embarcadero parade route were far too young to have any memory of the 49ers first Super Bowl championship, this Valkyries team has brought a similar feeling to the Bay Area. The 49ers helped bring San Francisco out of a very dark space, created by the Milk-Moscone murders at City Hall, the Jonestown tragedy in Guyana and somber days of a debilitating recession. Joe Montana and Ronnie Lott soothed the city's soul, made people proud to say they were from San Francisco. The Valkyries were born when the city was still being vilified by conservative pundits, struggling to recover from the pandemic, serving as a national punchline. Their two years of existence have coincided with the Trump administration's vicious attacks on the LGBTQ+ community, other marginalized groups and on women's rights. Which is why their victory party wasn't just about sports. It was a celebration of who we are. All of us. And particularly a celebration of women. This was our first sports party for a professional women's team, representing the half of society shut out of sports for too long. One that used love and friendship and the fight for equity as keys to victory. This is the first women's professional team to stand on the mountaintop with the Bay Area's other sports icons. item.description: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings (14) runs after a catch against the Indianapolis Colts in the fourth quarter on Oct. 25 in Minneapolis. (Bruce Kluckhohn/Associated Press) When head coach Kyle Shanahan was asked Wednesday about Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings reportedly declining a trade last week that would have sent him back to the San Francisco 49er s, Shanahan said the story didn't capture the full picture. "The report was accurate," he said, "just not totally exactly detailed up." What does that mean? Well, the part of the report from Fox's Jay Glazer that included how Jennings declined to get on a FaceTime call with Shanahan and general manager John Lynch , who were hoping to seal the deal? That was wrong, Shanahan said. Or, rather, not totally exactly detailed up. "It was actually - it was J.J. FaceTiming me," Shanahan said. "… It was a good talk, but he's with good people (in Minnesota). He likes where he's at. And I thought it made sense what he said and I agreed with him." That doesn't make total sense. Jennings has six catches on 10 targets in six games with a 6-1 team that values him so little that it's willing to trade him to a 6-1 team it could be battling for the NFC's No. 1 seed. And he's enjoying that situation so much that he declined a trade to his employer for his first six NFL seasons (2020-2025) that clearly still values him? It sounds like there's more to the story, possibly having to do with the 49ers not meeting Jennings' contract extension demands last year. Whatever the case, here's what the story - warts and all - tells us: The 49ers are in the market for a wide receiver before the NFL's trade deadline on Tuesday. Shanahan spoke Wednesday for the first time since the 49ers traded for Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner during last week's bye and said the 49ers might not be done dealing. His message contrasted with last year's when he downplayed deadline activity. At the deadline, the 49ers were 6-3, but had lost two All-Pros, pass rusher Nick Bosa and linebacker Fred Warner , to season-ending injuries. They made a low-wattage move, acquiring pass rusher Keion White from the Patriots in a swap of late-round picks. "I do know our team's better than it was last year," Shanahan said. item.title: Spurs fashion gets hairy as Keldon Johnson's mustache steals the show
item.description: Keldon Johnson arrives at the Frost Bank Center ahead of the matchup against the Dallas Mavericks. (Courtesy of San Antonio Spurs) Camouflage, flashy kicks and a mustache that deserves its own starting lineup. The San Antonio Spurs brought plenty of personality to the Frost Bank Center on Wednesday night, Nov. 4, ahead of their showdown with the Dallas Mavericks. From designer sneakers to statement graphic tees, the Silver and Black made sure their pregame fashion was anything but ordinary. Here's a closer look at what five Spurs players wore before tipoff. Forget wearing flashy clothes, Keldon Johnson's mustache might have been the biggest fashion statement of the night. The reigning Sixth Man of the Year arrived sporting a playful mustache that looked straight out of a 1970s detective show, giving his pregame appearance a little extra character. Johnson wore a white VALE FOREVER "Air Donald" graphic tee featuring Ronald McDonald soaring toward a basketball hoop, layered beneath a light-gray zip-up hoodie. He paired the outfit with blue jeans, Bottega Veneta Orbit low-top sneakers, and his signature "KJ" chain. Now, Stephon Castle kicked things off in a Boredom Kills Trust camouflage long-sleeve sweatshirt featuring a large graphic across the chest. The Spurs guard paired the sweatshirt with light-wash blue jeans and a cross necklace, keeping his look casual while letting the camouflage do the talking. It looks like Castle's "Area 51" teammate, Victor Wembanyama, also got the camouflage memo. At 7-foot-4, blending into a crowd isn't exactly Wembanyama's specialty, but the Spurs superstar gave it a shot Wednesday night, wearing a black zip-up hoodie layered beneath a Nike Tech Dri-FIT Woven Camo Windrunner Oversized Jacket in Neutral Olive and Black. He completed the look with gray Nike joggers and olive-green Nike sneakers, keeping things comfortable with an outdoors-inspired ensemble. With his hood up and hands tucked into his pockets, Wembanyama looked ready for a covert mission rather than an NBA matchup. Spurs guard Dylan Harper kept things coordinated in a forest-green Nike hoodie and matching sweatpants layered over a black T-shirt. He completed the outfit with black Nike sneakers and his signature diamond-encrusted No. 2 chain, adding some sparkle to his otherwise understated look. Between laid-back camouflage fits and colorful sweats, Johnson personality stands out the most as the Spurs get ready to face their in-state rival, the Dallas Mavericks. item.title: Cheboygan volleyball to face Kingsley in D2 district title match
item.description: GRAYLING — Cheboygan volleyball is back in the district final. Playing in an MHSAA Division 2 district semifinal clash on Wednesday, Nov. 4, the Chiefs kept their season alive by capturing a 3-0 victory at Grayling (25-23, 25-23, 25-23). CHEBOYGAN JV VOLLEYBALL FINISHES 41-0: Cheboygan JV volleyball team caps off perfect 41-0 season on court TUESDAY DISTRICT ROUNDUP: Mackinaw City, NMCA advance to MHSAA district volleyball finals DISTRICT VOLLEYBALL PREVIEW: Previewing, predicting Cheboygan-area volleyball district tournaments The Chiefs took a 21-16 lead in the first set after junior Sophia Naden delivered a kill. However, Grayling, which trailed 24-16, rattled off an 8-0 run to tie the set and put all the pressure on the Chiefs. But following a Grayling attacking error, Naden hammered home another kill to give Cheboygan a one-set lead. The Vikings responded impressively by building a 16-12 lead in the second, but the Chiefs countered with a 7-3 spurt that was capped off by a kill from junior Diem Schley, which tied things up at 19. The teams went back and forth during several points, but the Chiefs took the lead for good when another kill from Naden gave Cheboygan a one-point advantage, which was then followed by another point that gave the Chiefs the set and victory. Much like the second set, the Chiefs trailed for much of the third. However, a pivotal run helped them tie the set. Polishing off the Cheboygan win was Schley, whose match-winning kill was too much for Grayling to handle. With the victory, the Chiefs (18-14-4) travel to face Kingsley (47-5-1) in a 6 p.m. district final on Thursday, Nov. 5. The Stags, who won last year's Division 3 state title, swept the Chiefs in Cheboygan earlier this season. Cheboygan fell to Ogemaw Heights in a D2 district final last year. Stats from Cheboygan's match will be provided as soon as they become available. Contact sports editor Jared Greenleaf at jgreenleaf@gannett.com . item.title: How much Cleveland magic can pitching coach Joe Torres bring to Reds?
item.description: The Cincinnati Reds’ new pitching coach goes from one of the best pitching-developmental organizations of the past few decades to one of the worst-performing pitching staffs of the 2026 season. Now all he has to do is bring enough secret pitching sauce from Cleveland in his first year as a lead pitching coach to fix a Reds staff that needs to become one of the top staffs in the league again – without All-Star Hunter Greene – for the Reds to have any chance to compete in 2027. Reds Hall of Fame Piniella Baker Pair of former Reds managers on Hall of Fame ballot Welcome to Cincinnati, Joe Torres. Torres, 44, was hired by the Reds this week to replace Derek Johnson after spending the past five seasons as an assistant to highly regarded Carl Willis in Cleveland, where he worked under Reds manager Terry Francona for two of those seasons and where the Guardians’ pitching staff ranked among the top 10 in the majors all five years. “This being my first year in this lead position and having a manager with the experience that Tito has, that’s so comforting for me,” said Torres, who has less than four weeks to get to know a group of pitchers he has only seen from across the field before MLB owners impose an industry shutdown Dec. 1 with a widely anticipated labor lockout. “I’ve got a small time window here with getting to know guys,” Torres said on the day his hiring was announced, Nov. 4. “It’s getting to know them as a person first. I’ve got to get in there and see what makes them tick, what motivates them, and see where I can help them and help add value.” Injuries and underperformance – especially when it came to issuing walks and hitting guys – buried the pitching staff in 2026 and by extension the Reds chances to compete during a 75-87, last-place season. “We have got to work ahead (in the count),” Francona said during an interview later in the day on WLW-radio. “There were so many innings last year when even when we got through the inning there were a bunch of 3-2 counts (and high pitch totals). That’s not going to work out over the course of a game or the season. We’ve got to be more economical.” Reds pitchers led the majors in walks and were fourth in hit batters. Torres called that a “priority” and plans to start breaking down solutions as he gets to know his pitchers. “I’ve got to get in and see why (that happened). What was the reason for each individual?” he said. “That could be a delivery thing. item.title: ‘Inexcusable and Semi-Reprehensible,’ ‘You’re Ruining Your Players’ — Bill Simmons Rips Adam Silver’s ‘Negligence and Greed’ Over 82-Game Schedule
item.description: ‘Inexcusable and Semi-Reprehensible,’ ‘You’re Ruining Your Players’ — Bill Simmons Rips Adam Silver’s ‘Negligence and Greed’ Over 82-Game Schedule Bill Simmons wants the NBA to cut its regular season from 82 games to 70, and he blames Commissioner Adam Silver and the league’s owners for the current schedule. The Ringer founder made his case on Tuesday’s episode of “The Bill Simmons Podcast.” His argument also centered on potential expansion in Las Vegas and Seattle, which could bring billions in fees to the league’s current owners. Bill Simmons Targets Adam Silver Over NBA Schedule and Potential Expansion Fees The podcaster opened his criticism by directing it at the league office. “Listen, I don’t know how many times I’ve talked about this on the pod about the schedule and about how this, to me, is just inexcusable and semi-reprehensible that whoever is in charge of the league, which I think is Adam Silver these days, that he doesn’t care,” Simmons said . The NBA has maintained an 82-game regular season since 1967-68, apart from seasons shortened by labor disputes or other disruptions. He continued, “You’re ruining your players … and you’re hurting careers, and you’re shortening careers. This should be a 70-game season. And if you talk to literally everybody who plays basketball, all of them would say the season needs to be shorter. And if you don’t do it at this point, I just think it’s negligent. I really do. I think it’s actual negligence and greed.” The NBA has 30 franchises, and adding teams in Las Vegas and Seattle would mark its first expansion since the Charlotte Bobcats joined the league in 2004. That potential expansion is central to Simmons’ argument because of the money he expects the league’s current owners to receive. “The question for me is, you’re gonna make all this money … that’s gonna be $9.5 billion for the [Las Vegas] expansion team … They’re gonna get a second thing from Seattle, which is gonna be $7.5 (billion), something like that. … So all these owners are getting, I don’t know, $16 billion in expansion fees,” he said. Those figures are his estimates. In March, the New York Post reported that expansion fees could range from $7 billion to $10 billion per team, with the money going to the NBA’s current owners rather than being shared with players. Cutting 12 games from each team’s schedule would also mean fewer home dates and fewer opportunities to sell tickets and concessions. Simmons questioned why the league would resist cutting games despite that potential windfall. “And yet everyone’s like, ‘Well, we can’t lose games. We’d lose too much money. We’d lose revenue,'” he said. The NBA’s Board of Governors voted March 25 to explore expansion into Las Vegas and Seattle, although neither city has been awarded a franchise. item.title: Texans’ Will Anderson Jr. raises eyebrows with Justin Herbert take before Chargers game
item.description: Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Texans’ Will Anderson Jr. raises eyebrows with Justin Herbert take before Chargers game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Houston Texans defensive end Will Anderson Jr. had some high praise for Justin Herbert ahead of Sunday’s matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers . However, his assessment of the quarterback’s current play might leave NFL fans wondering what he has been watching. "Herbert, man, he's playing out of his mind." Will Anderson Jr. on facing Justin Herbert and the Chargers. pic.twitter.com/e0kbBySPrC Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — NFL Network (@nflnetwork) November 4, 2026 “He is still a really great quarterback in this league… he is still a very respectable player in this league. We have a ton of respect for him. We know what to expect a little bit. But Herbert, man, he’s playing out of his mind.” The first part of Anderson’s comments are fine. But the last part of the praise isn’t factually correct at this point in Herbert’s career. The Chargers are 0-7, and Herbert has struggled to find consistency in Mike McDaniel’s offense. He has looked uncomfortable in the scheme and made questionable decisions. He and McDaniel are failing to get the most out of an offense that was expected to take a step forward. Los Angeles now faces another difficult test against a Houston defense that has given Herbert problems in the past. Anderson and his teammates will have an opportunity to make those struggles continue, especially if the Chargers cannot find a way to get their quarterback comfortable. It’s been a rough season for Houston, but this can be a bounceback game. The Chargers need Herbert to look more like the quarterback Anderson described, but that has not happened through seven games. item.title: Rece Davis: CFP rankings show ‘needs to be reimagined’ when bracket expands to 24
item.description: Credit: ESPN If the College Football Playoff rankings show feels like a chore with a 12-team field, just imagine how it will be with 24 teams starting next season. After the heavily criticized first rankings release of the season on ESPN this week, host Rece Davis deftly avoided direct criticism of the selection committee while noting on The Pat McAfee Show that he expected significant turnover among the teams going forward. Davis is tasked with interviewing committee chair Hunter Yurachek about the list each week, and creating some semblance of a track record over the course of the season. In a follow-up conversation Wednesday on The College GameDay Podcast , Davis expressed uncertainty over the future of the rankings show. “If this continues … I don’t know that the show itself continues. I assume it will, because it’s still under the original contract,” he said. “But it will certainly feel different. It felt different when we went to 12 a couple of years ago, it’s certainly going to feel different when we go to 24.” While insider Pete Thamel confirmed that he expects the rankings show will continue under the CFP’s updated agreement with ESPN , Davis acknowledged the show could become very dry running through two-dozen teams. The longtime College GameDay host suggested the show should not air any rankings beyond 25 even once the tournament expands, and offered the idea of perhaps starting with the first team out to build suspense. “It probably needs to be reimagined,” he said. “I mean, are we really going to start … at 35? But then people are like, ‘Let’s go.’ So I think if you start at 25, [it’s], ‘OK here’s the first team out.’ Maybe you do it like that.” The show draws millions of viewers and theoretically helps the CFP selection committee hold itself accountable. However, it has become a source of tension at ESPN and in the industry. Star commentator Kirk Herbstreit bowed out from the broadcast early on , and in-house critics such as Michael Wilbon have railed against the rankings show. When the field doubles in size , ESPN could have a different issue on its hands. The show could simply become too boring or monotonous for fans. Get off. We understand your feelings; whether right or wrong, you reflect me in the biggest and most important ways. Whatever you say might as well come out of my mouth and be on my Twitter. Get the wives off of Twitter; it’s damaging.” Then, what Ward had to say next could stir up some more drama. item.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - OCTOBER 14: Soccer player and World champion Lothar Matthäus attends the SKY Preview of "Müller-Wohlfahrt - Der Arzt der Champions" on October 14, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Gisela Schober/Getty Images) | Getty Images Lothar Matthäus has come out strongly in defense of Michael Olise, firmly rejecting suggestions that Bayern Munich should fine the 24-year-old French winger following his sending-off during Champions League action against Viking FK. While acknowledging that Olise’s red card in Norway proved costly in the 3-3 d raw, the Bayern legend argued that missing the upcoming European fixture against Arsenal is punishment enough for a player driven purely by playing the gam e. “Why would I think about fining Olise [following his red card], as it has been suggested? item.description: Jerry Jones and Cowboys linked to star edge rusher before trade deadline originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Cowboys are in freefall after their 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 8 of the NFL season. Now, this team is 3-5 and in a pinch to turn things around quickly. So, what's a team to do? Owner and general manager Jerry Jones is known for making big moves before the trade deadline, so it's certainly not a far-fetched idea. The NFL trade deadline is coming up on Nov. 10, so now is the time for Jones to make one of his famous splashy moves. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have released a piece with some of the latest talk around the NFL ahead of the trade deadline . Dallas Cowboys could target Cardinals star Josh Sweat before trade deadline In the piece, Fowler links the Cowboys to a star edge rusher. It's not a totally crazy idea, of course, since that's one position the Cowboys have had their eye on for a long time. "Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat has been linked to Dallas, which could be in the pass rush market but hasn't made any moves there yet," Fowler says. "The sense I get from teams in the edge rusher market is that Sweat would prefer a new deal as part of a trade -- or at least a sweetener, such as a raise on his $18.1 million salary this year or next." He adds, "He's in the second year of a four-year, $76 million contract, so wanting it reworked so early in the deal could be a hurdle to a trade." It's not Maxx Crosby, but the Cowboys could make a move for another star edge rusher before too long.
